A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cholesky product-geometry framework, with identifiable corresponding metrics, theorems, experiments, and appendices. The scientific material supports reliable comparison. The failed acronym list in v2 is a presentation defect rather than an essential evidence gap.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original numerical-stability simulations, tensor-interpolation results, and SPDNet accuracy and timing experiments on Radar and HDM05.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original classifier, residual-network, stability, interpolation, sensitivity, diagonal-distribution, and scalability results.

M1.justification: The core metrics, deformations, operators, and MLR formulas are retained: CDEM and CDBWM become PCM and BWCM. The procedural extensions are residual blocks using the proposed exponential maps (Section 5, Eq. 16) and an evaluated variant learning diagonal M instead of fixing it to the identity (Appendix E.6).

E1.justification: Radar, HDM05, numerical-stability simulations, and tensor interpolation remain. V2 adds FPHA, extending action-recognition coverage to first-person hand actions: 1,175 sequences across 45 categories (Appendix E.1.2). Additional backbones primarily broaden evaluation within these retained classification tasks.

E2.justification: The SPDNet classifier comparison expands from vanilla SPDNet and LCM in v1 Table 6 to AIM, LEM, and LCM in v2 Table 2; the vanilla SPDNet result is removed. V2 also evaluates these competing geometries in GyroSPD and residual networks, and includes PEM and BWM in the new MLR runtime comparison (Table 13).

E3.justification: V2 replaces the sparse positive deformation choices with a sweep from -2 to 1.5 and different selected parameters. It adds one-block HDM05 evaluation, GyroSPD and residual-network protocols, and FPHA-specific preprocessing. Stability testing adds theta=0.15 and extends the smallest diagonal values from 1e-15 to 1e-30. Appendix E.5 introduces a 50-class, batch-30 forward/backward timing protocol over dimensions 32–512.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's stability, interpolation, and limited deformation comparisons, v2 adds systematic theta sweeps (Tables 9–10), fixed-versus-learned M ablations (Table 14), input/output diagonal-distribution analysis (Figure 3), and dimensional scalability tests (Table 13). Expanded stability tests investigate failure closer to the logarithmic-metric limit. The original interpolation analysis is retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Classifier summaries change from ten-fold averages in v1 to five-fold results in v2, retaining the plus/minus reporting format. V1's explicit randomized-initialization and split statement is no longer supplied. The new residual-network comparison reports the best of three trials without uncertainty intervals (v2 Table 4). These are reported aggregation changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive classifier, residual-network, sensitivity, scalability, and learned-M results. Its expanded stability table reports 100% failure for theta=0.15 DBWM at 1e-30, whereas v1 tested only theta=0.5 and 1.5 with zero failures. Retained stability entries also change, including the 256-dimensional CM/DLM result at 1e-1 from 14.05% to 14.29%. Classifier results use changed theta and repetition settings, preventing same-setting improvement claims. Interpolation determinants remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds an analytical comparison of matrix-function counts and per-sample computational costs for seven MLR geometries (Appendix E.5.1, Tables 11–12). Definition 3.1 explicitly formalizes weighted coordinate metrics. The principal metric, deformation, gyro-structure, and MLR results are retained, with their proofs largely relocated to Appendix F.

C1.justification: Both versions claim two Cholesky/SPD metric families with efficient, stable, closed-form operators. V2 extends the stated contributions to constructing residual blocks and elevates neural-network applications alongside the geometric contributions. The central metric-design and novelty claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 substantially extends v1's explanation that powers distort diagonal entries less than logarithms. It proposes dataset-specific explanations using diagonal imbalance, explains BWCM's greater tolerance of negative theta, interprets the limited benefit of learning M, and explicitly identifies instability near the logarithmic limit (Section 6.2 and Appendices E.3–E.6). These add mechanisms and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: V1 already specifies SPDNet widths, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and epochs. V2 adds detailed GyroSPD covariance construction, residual-network settings, FPHA processing, selected theta values, and the parameterization and initialization of learned M. Appendix E.7 newly discloses CPU, GPU, and memory information. Both versions advertise code, although v2 inconsistently also says release will follow acceptance.

R1.justification: The introduction shifts from broad SPD-geometry applications toward metrics as building blocks for neural networks. It adds substantial positioning around residual networks, diffusion and flow models, and recent normalization and attention research, including Katsman et al. (2024), Li et al. (2024), and Chen and Lipman (2024). The foundational relationship to Lin's Cholesky geometry remains.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative. Main-text theory is condensed and reorganized, proofs move to Appendix F, the existing MLR theorem moves into Section 5, and interpolation moves into Appendix E.2. An appendix contents page and reproducibility, ethics, and language-model disclosures are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds a framework diagram and diagonal-distribution plots, restructures accuracy/timing tables, expands the stability grid, and introduces sensitivity and scalability tables. The original interpolation figure and determinant table are relocated rather than newly generated evidence. The conference layout replaces the manuscript format, but the new acronym-list page visibly contains a LaTeX glossary-generation error.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's limited learning validation through AIM/LEM comparisons, additional architectures and FPHA, and systematic deformation, learned-M, and scalability analyses. Identifying a stability failure boundary also makes the practical claims more informative. These gains outweigh fewer reported folds, best-of-three residual reporting, an overbroad GyroSPD superiority statement—BWCM trails LCM on Radar in Table 3—and the broken acronym list. The improvement comes principally from stronger validation and interpretation, while the core geometry remains stable.
